items.title: BMI's limits for athletes
items.claim: Body Mass Index (Quetelet, 1830s; popularised in the 20th century) is a single number from mass over height squared. Why is it problematic for athletes?

options.text: It does not distinguish lean mass from fat mass, so muscular athletes are often classified overweight or obese
It is unrelated to body shape

items.reveal:
Rugby forwards, weightlifters and bodybuilders routinely fall above the 'overweight' or 'obese' threshold despite low body fat.

DXA, hydrostatic weighing and skinfolds give better composition data for performance contexts.
items.why: Population-level measures and individual measures answer different questions.

items.title: Static stretching before exercise
items.claim: Sports science guidance on pre-exercise static stretching changed substantially. What do current consensus reviews say?

options.text: Static stretching pre-exercise reliably reduces injury and improves performance
Long static holds before power activities can reduce subsequent performance; dynamic warm-up is generally preferred
No warm-up of any kind is recommended

items.reveal_title: Pre-exercise long static holds can hurt power output
items.reveal:
Reviews (Behm and Chaouachi, 2011; Behm et al., 2016) summarise that holds longer than around 60 seconds before sprint or jump activities can transiently reduce performance.

Dynamic warm-ups are now standard in elite team-sport protocols.
items.why: Practice guidelines often persist in coaching long after research has moved on.

items.title: Where the Paralympics began
items.claim: The Paralympic movement traces back to which institution and clinician?

options.text: Stoke Mandeville Hospital, UK, with Ludwig Guttmann's 1948 games for spinal-injured veterans

items.reveal:
Guttmann staged archery contests for World War II veterans with spinal cord injuries on the opening day of the London 1948 Olympics.

The first Paralympic Games proper were held in Rome in 1960.
items.why: Para-sport began as a rehabilitative intervention, not a sporting tradition.
